subject: Sequencing conflict between MAP gates — ownership and next steps
messages:
From: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@kestrelretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Jordan —

Quick question after reviewing the latest MAP you shared (thank you). There are two critical gating items that look like they are ordered in parallel but in practice Kestrel needs them sequentially:

- Kestrel legal signs the contract (procurement)
- Kestrel IT completes the network allowlist and hands back API keys

From past on-prem and private plans, your IT team prefers to finish the allowlist and confirm connectivity before procurement will trigger payment milestones. If that’s the case we should swap the order in the MAP so the delivery milestones (API credentials + test calls) occur prior to the billing milestone.

That shift affects the close date by 5–7 business days. I don’t want to surprise finance or our AE; Laura/Ben, can we confirm whether we can: (a) provide a temporary scoped API key for staging so IT can validate connectivity without legal signature, or (b) accept a conditional SOW that lets IT start while procurement finishes?

Jordan, can you confirm Kestrel’s preference ASAP? If we need to re-sequence I’ll update the MAP and a minimal risk log to track the change.

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Kestrel_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@kestrelretail.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@globalretail.com>, it-ops@kestrelretail.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Thanks Priyom —

Apologies for the delay. Short answer: procurement wants signatures before any production access. Our IT can do allowlist work and provide test IPs, but they will not approve an API key until legal signs. If you can provide a timeboxed staging key (no data persistence, rate-limited) for validation, that is often an acceptable compromise; procurement still requires signature before production keys.

If we keep the MAP as-is, the procurement signature becomes the gating item and the close will effectively move to when our CPO signs off — likely 7 business days from today given internal reviews.

Jordan
VP Product, Kestrel Retail
From: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@kestrelretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity. Laura/Ben: can we provide a timeboxed staging key and document the constraints (no retention, single-account scoping, strict rate limits)? Neha, this will touch security/compliance because we’ll be issuing scoped credentials pre-contract — any red flags for SOC2/contractual wording?

If we do staging keys, proposed plan:
1) Issue staging key to Kestrel IT (scoped, TTL 7 days) — allows connectivity and final integration test
2) Kestrel procurement completes signature window (target: +7 business days)
3) On signature, swap staging key to production keys and trigger first invoice

If staging keys are disallowed, we will need to move the billing milestone to post-signature and update the MAP; that adjustment adds risk on the close date and impacts our delivery runway.

I’ll prepare an updated MAP draft once we confirm the path.

—Priyom
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Team —

Security position: we can support scoped, non-persistent staging credentials with the following mandatory controls:
- TTL 7 days, auto-expire and rotate
- No data retention (sandbox mode) and read-only logs exported to a separated S3 bucket with 30-day retention
- IP allowlist to Kestrel test bed only
- Signed Acknowledgement from Kestrel IT accepting limited functionality and no SLA for staging

We need a short one-off addendum to the MAP that documents these controls. Legal should sign that addendum locally; it does not replace the main contract. If accepted, this mitigates the schedule slip risk by allowing integration work to proceed.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@kestrelretail.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@globalretail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Jordan —

We can do the staging path per Neha’s constraints. I’ve attached a short addendum (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf reference) and an updated MAP that sequences: 1) IT validation with staging key (7d window), 2) procurement signature, 3) production key issuance + invoice.

Operational impact: staging path reduces close delay to ~2 business days (time to set up TTL keys + IT validation) versus the 7-day procurement-first scenario.

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm Kestrel IT can accept the addendum and sign the acknowledgement (today)
- Marta/Procurement: If acceptable, please countersign the addendum so we can ship the staging key tomorrow

If we don’t get acknowledgement by EOD, we should accept a +7 business day close slide and trigger the risk log entry.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@globalretail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@kestrelretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sequencing question — API keys vs procurement signature

Laura/Priyom —

Procurement reviewed the addendum and IT acknowledgement. We will sign the staging acknowledgement today but want the MAP updated to show explicit acceptance criteria for IT validation (test calls x3, latency <200ms, allowlist confirmation). Once those are in the MAP we’ll countersign the main SOW within 3 business days.

We appreciate the flexible approach — countersigning the acknowledgement mitigates a longer close slip. Please update the MAP and the risk register to capture: owner = Redwood (Priyom), impact = medium (close slip reduced), contingency = rollback to procurement-first and updated invoice timing.

Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Kestrel Retail
